title: Replace the brake fluid
summary: Flush old, moisture-filled brake fluid out of a hydraulic brake and bleed it with fresh fluid.
tools: Box wrench for the bleed valve
Clear hose that fits the bleed valve
parts: Sealed new brake fluid (DOT type on your spec sheet)

steps.text: Turn the handlebar so the brake reservoir sits level, and cover the paint and plastics around it with rags.
steps.caution: Brake fluid strips paint and damages plastic. Wipe drips immediately and rinse with water.

steps.text: Open the reservoir cover and remove the diaphragm. Note the fluid's color; dark fluid is overdue.
Fit the clear hose to the caliper's bleed valve and run it into the catch bottle.
Squeeze and hold the brake lever, open the bleed valve a quarter turn, then close it before you release the lever. Repeat.
Keep topping up the reservoir with fresh fluid as you go. Continue until clean, bubble-free fluid comes through the hose.
steps.caution: Never let the reservoir run dry, or air enters the line and you have to start over.

steps.text: Tighten the bleed valve, fill the reservoir to the upper line and refit the diaphragm and cover.
Pump the lever. It should feel firm and stop well short of the grip. Test the brake at walking pace before riding.
steps.caution: If the lever still feels spongy, don't ride. Bleed again or have a shop do it. Bikes with ABS may need a dealer tool to bleed fully.
